articleTitle: Quasi-universal VLSI multiplier with signed digit arithmetic
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 1987 IEEE Southern Tier Technical Conference, 1987.
abstract: This paper presents techniques to increase the speed and improve the VLSI suitability in designing fixed-point multipliers. The implementation of high-speed multiplication algorithm using redundant binary addition tree has been investigated and a minimal logic design of Redundant Binary Signed-Digit (RBSD) adder cell is presented. The regular interconnects on structures of these adder cells result in a multiplier which is ideal for VLSI implementation. The increased speed is achieved through carry free addition of partial products using redundant signed-digit numbers. The use of multiplier recoding scheme with a group size of three, which will reduce the number of rows in the partial product matrix by a factor of three, is discussed. The complexity introduced by this recoding scheme is the need for multiples of -3 and +3 of the multiplicand which involves carry propagation free adders for these precalculation units in conventional designs. This scheme results in a significant improvement in speed and is very efficient for multipliers with large operand lengths.

articleTitle: Direct Computation of the Polynomial Expression Ax/sup 2/ + Bx + C
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 1987 IEEE Southern Tier Technical Conference, 1987.
abstract: The present study focuses on the realization of the polynomial expression Ax/sup 2/ + Bx + C. The computation of the polynomial expression is achieved in a parallel and pipelined structure with time and hardware savings if compared to a direct realization of the expression with explicit calculations. The layout of the hardware is simple, given the uniformity of matrices, thus suitable for VLSI design.

articleTitle: Optical Detection of Rent Pins in a High-Density Array
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 1987 IEEE Southern Tier Technical Conference, 1987.
abstract: This paper describes a prototype system being developed for the detection of bent pins on a high density integrated circuit module. It is a noncontact approach that relies on the detection of the specific optical diffraction patterns that result when laser light shines on a bent pin. As the module pins are passed through a fixed laser beam, the diffraction patterns are captured by an area optical array which is continuously scanned by a dedicated processor. If a bent pin is detected and the motion of the pin array is known, the approximate location of the bent pin can be determined by triangulation based on multiple passes. Information revealing the angle of bend in the scanning plane is imbedded in the diffraction pattern.

articleTitle: On the Optimal Pulse Control of an Electric Drive
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 1987 IEEE Southern Tier Technical Conference, 1987.
abstract: Results on the application of an optimal control technique in microprocessor-based position control system with a DC motor are presented. The technique is based on the use of optimal control corresponding to various "typical" initial conditions, defined during the system design and stored in a look-up table. A numerical procedure for the definition of optimal control signals is proposed.

articleTitle: Voice Recognition - the Next Generation Man-Machine Input Device?
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 1987 IEEE Southern Tier Technical Conference, 1987.
abstract: As the complexity of today's cockpit increases, so does the workload of the pilot. The common keyboard is no longer an acceptable stand-alone input device for today's high-performance aircraft. Instead, new man-machine interface technologies must be produced to alleviate the pilot from extreme workload conditions. Particularly in fighter aircraft, the pilot needs a method of hands-free and eyes-free communication. Voice technology offers potential for reducing the pilot's visual and manual workload. This paper describes advantages and disadvantages of voice recognition systems and takes a brief look at the state of development of voice technology.

articleTitle: Innovative Helical Wrap Installation of Fiber Optic Cable
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 1987 IEEE Southern Tier Technical Conference, 1987.
abstract: A fiber optic link, spun helically onto a phase conductor and lightning shield (static) wire of an existing 115KV transmission line, replaces an unreliable direct current. Pilot wire relay channel in a developmental project of the NYSEG Corporation. The resulting installation, now completed, was the first of its kind in the U.S. and is the first anywhere that employs a fiber cable helically wrapped around a lightning shield wire.

articleTitle: A Simplified Self-Checking Design of Multioutput Circuits
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 1987 IEEE Southern Tier Technical Conference, 1987.
abstract: In this paper,a new error-control technique for multioutput circuits is given. This technique uses two-rail code and Exclusive-OR functions to monitor the outputs of multioutput circuits. The design scheme has better efficiency than the existing schemes because it can detect multiple errors and gives the error indication immediately and the redundancy used is much lower. The detailed analysis of error characteristics and error coverage of this scheme are given. The methods for designing and minimizing the redundancy are presented.

articleTitle: Multiplier Design Using Signed-Digit Number System
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 1987 IEEE Southern Tier Technical Conference, 1987.

articleTitle: Locating Signal Line Defects with Thermal Image Analysis
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 1987 IEEE Southern Tier Technical Conference, 1987.
abstract: Plated circuit lines in printed circuit boards have been known to have certain faults which can cause electrical signal problems. One of these faults is a near-open (circuit line which has normal resistance but has defects which cause changes in the electrical signal). To detect the location of these faults, an experiment was conducted utilizing a Thermal Image Analyzer (TIA). The results show that this technique is feasible. This report details the experiment.

articleTitle: A Computer Controlled Aircraft Defense System (CCADS)
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 1987 IEEE Southern Tier Technical Conference, 1987.
abstract: The problems and complexities of defending military aircraft from hostile forces are described. Many different types of weapon systems may be encountered, requiring rapid, accurate countermeasures for survival. It is shown how computer generation of a tactical situation display and computer control of aircraft sensors and countermeasures enhances aircraft survival, compared to autonomous or manual approaches.

articleTitle: Low-cost Microcomputer Networking: Some Practical Considerations
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 1987 IEEE Southern Tier Technical Conference, 1987.
abstract: The perceived need to network office computers is often overstated. Evaluation of needs and device characteristics often leads to a simpler, lower cost solution. Frequently, needs are satisfied by the low-cost networks or even manual processes. The reasons for networking are discussed and analyzed in terms of some practical constraints. The characteristics and capabilities of the low-cost networks are described and a decision guide is presented.

articleTitle: Speech Recognition: A TutoriaI on the Subject
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 1987 IEEE Southern Tier Technical Conference, 1987.
abstract: The unnatural form of communication that one must use in interaction with a computer has prompted much research in the area of voice recognition. There have been enormous amounts of research in this area in the past decade. This paper presents a simplified overview of the linguistics and system approach behind speech recognition systems, so that those unfamiliar with this area may obtain a generalized understanding of the setbacks, achievements and operation of the verbal interface.

articleTitle: Computer machine contol language development
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 1987 IEEE Southern Tier Technical Conference, 1987.
abstract: This paper presents the architecture, structure, and general development of a computer machine control language. A specific language development is presented for a general purpose educational robot. The machine control primitives are identified and defined. The necessary functional control of the robot is identified and the primitives are used to derive secondary control expressions at a higher level. The utility of the higher level language is used for support, control, sensing, and development, while the machine primitive manipulation is delegated to lower levels of the language hierarchy. This approach to developing the computer control software bridges the gap between the convenience and efficiency of the high level user support and the labor of manipulating the machine control and sensing primitives.

articleTitle: On the Optimization of Search Heuristics: A Fuzzy Approach
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 1987 IEEE Southern Tier Technical Conference, 1987.
abstract: Heuristics are key factors in reducing the computational workload of searching decision trees. Artificial intelligence techniques utilize algorithms which are highly dependent upon the heuristic sensitivity and the processing workload required to generate the plausibility of a given node. Fuzzy set theory offers a means of providing reasonable heuristics to the search procedure in an effort to improve overall heuristic performance. A procedure was defined to generate fuzzy heuristics for an nth order state-space system. Results indicate that although the fuzzy heuristic is more sensitive than a linear-weighted test heuristic and may be beneficial for certain applications, the defuzzification algorithm required by the fuzzy approach required increased computational efforts. A brief review of AI search techniques is provided as well as an illustrative example which compares the performance of the fuzzy heuristic versus a linear-weighted test heuristic.

articleTitle: Quasi-Universal VLSI Multiplier with Signed Digit Arithmetic
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 1987 IEEE Southern Tier Technical Conference, 1987.
abstract: An algorithm is proposed for the design of a quasi-universal multiplier, i.e. one that can multiply two binary numbers and yield, upon instruction specification, the product in sign magnitude, two's complement or one's complement notation. The partial product matrix is created with direct multiplication and then reduced with signed digit additions.

articleTitle: A Generalized Approach for Automatic Test Pattern Generation
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 1987 IEEE Southern Tier Technical Conference, 1987.
abstract: A generalized approach for designing fault simulators using a library of simulation primitives is presented in this paper. A comprehensive set of simulation primitives has been developed using C programming language on the IBM PC. This library of simulation primitives has been used in realizing a fault simulator for automatic test pattern generation in combinational logic circuits. The fault simulator employs a combination of random pattern generation, concurrent fault simulation, and FAN algorithm for generating the complete set of test vectors to cover all the faults in the fault dictionary of the circuit under test. The library of simulation primitives is general enough to facilitate the development of fault simulators using any other test algorithms such as DALG or PODEM.

articleTitle: a Practical Reliability Evaluation of Embedded Avionic Software
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 1987 IEEE Southern Tier Technical Conference, 1987.
abstract: The implementation of multiple microprocessor based flight control systems has provided new highs of hardware reliability. Current design goals for system reliability are in the order of 10 to 50 thousand hours. The need to consider failure of software in the system MTBF calculations has arisen, even though software doesn't "fail" in the traditional hardware sense. The current state of the art in software reliability prediction badly lags that of the hardware sense. The current approach is to use multiple independently developed, software programs to eliminate the generic software fault in multi-processor systems. A side effect is to increase the cost of the software portion of a system. The General Electric Aerospace Control Systems Department has developed several flight control programs that have been in service for years, and some system failure data is examined in detail with respect to software faults. The results show that reliable software systems can be met with well tested and maintained single software designs. After one million flight hours in the field, one system exhibits continued reliability growth, with ten thousand hours MTBF for the software. The failures were all non-critical and include incorrect requirements as well as design and implementation errors. Over sixty percent of the failures were traced to incorrect requirements. The implementation of a reliable, well tested single software design system is a cost effective alternative to costly multiple "independent" program developments. Recent developments show unexpected correlation of errors in independently developed software designs, reducing expected improvements in reliability. This, coupled with the significant portion of errors imbedded in requirements, points toward well tested single software designs as a method of meeting software reliability requirements. Current FAA certification philosophy is open-minded on the single software design approach.

articleTitle: Utility Application of Static Var Compensation
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 1987 IEEE Southern Tier Technical Conference, 1987.
abstract: The Marcy South Project, 200 miles of 345KV (kilovolts) transmission lines, is-being constructed to permit the cost-effective north-south transfer of low cost hydro-produced power from Canada, downstate to New York City by 1988. This project has involved new and interesting technology in its design and construction. One such technology, soon to be implemented at New York State Electric & Gas (NYSEG), on a scale unprecedented in North America, is the Static Var Compensator (SVC). This paper describes NYSEG's SVC, a multi-million dollar power electronics technology not only new to NYSEG, but relatively new to the entire electric power industry. The various component parts of the SVC are discussed: thyristor valves, high voltage shunt capacitors, shunt reactors, harmonic filters, and the microcomputer controller. Basically, a gigantic parallel tuned circuit at 345KV, the SVC will regulate the voltage and enhance damping of power system oscillations, by controlling reactive power flow on the Bulk Power Transmission System in the area of Fraser, New York, in NYSEG's Oneonta District. This regulation and damping ability is critical to the stability and operability of the New York State Bulk Power System at the high levels of power transfer anticipated.

articleTitle: Image Recognition Procedure in an Adaptive Control System Applied to a Robotic Manipulator
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 1987 IEEE Southern Tier Technical Conference, 1987.
abstract: An approach aimed at the development and implementation of simplified adaptive control laws for robotic manipulators is presented. This approach maintains high performance of positioning systems of a manipulator despite variations of its load conditions and configuration by the use of a set of standard controllers, covering the expected range of variable system parameters. The simplified adaptation procedure, based on the image recognition technique, implies the selection of an appropriate controller for the particular operational conditions of the manipulator.

articleTitle: Software Development -- from Concept to Completion
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 1987 IEEE Southern Tier Technical Conference, 1987.
abstract: A large software development project is described with the steps taken toward completion. The software system was developed to support a new testing technology for digital computer designers. This software system was also required to fit into an existing, complex design automation system in IBM. The history of this design automation project over a three-year period and its characteristics are presented. The techniques used in development from initial modeling and requirement definition through shipment of code to the customers are identified. Techniques included are: development documentation, project planning, technical review meetings, automated testing tools, and formal inspections. Also discussed are some lessons learned. Changing requirements were all too common. While project planning was key, the critical factor was component staging from specification and development through testing and shipment. Management and technical awareness of the challenges were achieved through technical meetings. This led to the realization that the development process must change. Management and development perspectives were blended in this paper.

articleTitle: The Nesc, Probability, Reliability and the Future
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 1987 IEEE Southern Tier Technical Conference, 1987.
abstract: Papers on transmission line loadings published during the last twenty-five years have been sensitive to failure events as they consider discrete design loadings. In this period, five editions of the National Electric Safety Code (NESC) were published. The technical groups recommend "in vogue" design philosophy to determine loads. The NESC responds to "user" requests to change specific rules, and attempts to contain the effect of the change to the specific Rule. This paper presents excerpts from several committee reports on loads and follows with a parallel review of NESC Section 25 on Loadings and Section 26 on Strength. A discussion of overload Capacity Factor, Safety Factor, Structure Testing, and the relation of material factors to ultimate or rated breaking strength follow. The conclusion suggests that a joint effort by a Code and Technical Committee task force could result in a recommendation to modify the NESC to identify more rational design loads and load combinations, and place responsibility for utilization of material strength on engineers familiar with the latest technology.

articleTitle: Designing Testable Plas for both Offline Testing and Concurrent Error Detection
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 1987 IEEE Southern Tier Technical Conference, 1987.
abstract: In this paper, we present an improved design of testable PLAs for offline testing and suggest a unified approach for both offline testing and Concurrent Error Detection (CED). This design offers a more efficient use of the additional hardware for designing testable PLAs. The additional hardware required includes an address decoder [1] to select or deselect the product lines of the PLA, a ripple counter to generate the address for the decoder, and a Totally Self Checking checker for the output lines of the PLA. The design requires only two additional pinouts on the chip in contrast to (log/sub 2/(m+1)+1) additional pinouts where m is the number of product lines in the PLA. The additional hardware used for CED is also effectively utilized during offline testing, and the design is suitable for built-in testing of PLAs. The test procedures cover all single mode stuck-at, bridging, and crosspoint faults.

articleTitle: Innovative Variable Mesh Simulator
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 1987 IEEE Southern Tier Technical Conference, 1987.
abstract: A valuable design tool to aid designers of digital computer circuits is a "good" logic simulator. Because the digital hardware technology has advanced rapidly over recent years (i.e., more and more logic gates on a single chip), faster and easier to use logic simulators capable of handling large, complex digital circuits are continually in demand. An important milestone in meeting this demand was the development of the Innovative Variable Mesh Simulator (IVMS). The IVMS program is based on the flat model approach and permits interactive or batch processing. An earlier logic simulator called the Variable Mesh Simulator (VMS) is based on the hierarchical model approach and only permits batch processing. The use of the flat model approach in IVMS instead of the hierarchical approach in VMS results in a faster simulation for the same application. In addition to the processing advantages, interactive IVMS provides logic designers with the means to debug within a short period of time both the test case problems and the structure (the overall design and/or the individual behavior models). IVMS permits the user to explore various model changes and/or stimuli changes with the resulting output effects while in the same session. A more detailed description of the IVMS program development is given in this paper, including a comparison of the flat model and hierarchical models' approaches of simulator construction. The key features of the IVMS program, including some examples of performance data, are also described.

articleTitle: Fatigue and Creep in Solder Joints
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 1987 IEEE Southern Tier Technical Conference, 1987.
abstract: With the advent of surface mount components, many packaging engineers have been trying to determine the critical performance parameters for the technology. From first principals, the shear strain on a joint will be decreased if the distance between the components is increased. A simple way to do this is to increase the solder volume of the connection then fatigue cycle the parts to failure. The above experiment was performed with four different chip capacitors and six different solder volumes. The tests data confirmed a very consistent and predictable increase in fatigue life with solder joint height. Another item of interest to a package design engineer is how failures are initiated in a surface mount package. The usual assumption is that the only cause for failure is due to fatigue from dissimilar expansion coefficients of the components. Experiments have been performed the show solder cracking will occur in the solder due to the difference in expansion coefficients between the solder and component. No external loading is necessary. The size of the joint may have to be considered to minimize the problem.

articleTitle: On the Stability Analysis of an Adaptive Control System with a Simplified Control Procedure
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 1987 IEEE Southern Tier Technical Conference, 1987.
abstract: This paper presents the results on the stability analysis of computer-based control systems with the simplified adaptation procedure implemented through look-up tables and special selection rules. The simplified procedure implies the development of a number of controllers during the system design, representation of the controllers by a look-up table, and implementation of a procedure for the selection of the appropriate entry of a look-up table during the system operation. Systems, implementing the procedure, can be considered as systems with nonlinearity so that some specific stability problems have to be investigated. The paper presents the analysis of the transient processes in the system causes by the controller change, and the selection of the admissible difference between the alternative controllers in the look-up table. The analytical technique employed to the stability problem in the paper is based on Liapwnov's second method. Since the considered nonlinearity type meets Aizerman's conditions, a Liapunov function in so-called "Quadratic Plus Integral" was used. Following the general procedure of Liapunov's method, the absolute stability conditions were formulated for the considered type of control systems.

articleTitle: Gummel-Poon Model Parameter Optimization for a Power Transistor
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 1987 IEEE Southern Tier Technical Conference, 1987.
abstract: Computer Aided and Analysis tools rely heavily on accurate device models. The development of an accurate PNP power transistor model is presented in this paper. The device is modeled in terms of the Gummel-Poon model. It is difficult to obtain accurate values for the parameters due to the complexity of the model and the inherent assumptions and inaccuracies in the measurement procedure. Optimizing the parameter values through trial and error is not easy and a more systematic and efficient method is presented. An interactive design optimization program called DESIGN is used to adjust the parameter values so that the measured and the predicted output characteristics match at selected values of base current. The result is an accurate model that is sophisticated enough to predict the complex behavior of the transistor.

articleTitle: Programmable Placement Pressure in a Placement Head for Surface Mounted Devices
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 1987 IEEE Southern Tier Technical Conference, 1987.
abstract: Due to the broad spectrum of lead configurations of surface mount components and the variation in adhesive viscosities, various placement pressures are required. A proper adhesive meniscus must be achieved during application of components to adhesive dots to insure good lead to pad contact. This paper focuses on the development of a programmable placement pressure system which is a feature of the 4621A Omniplace Surface Mount Component Placement System. A commercially available pressure regulator is programmed with a DAC to produce the required back pressure for a piston activated compliant placement spindle. Coinciding with this, the Z axis servo system drives the placement spindle to the desired placement location. When the component, which is held by vacuum on the placement spindle, makes contact with the printed circuit board, a switch is activated. The computer receives the switch input as a signal to stop the Z axis drive. Pressure overshoot is avoided by the fast response time of the pressure regulator which controls the piston and the unique control algorithm which was developed. Included in this paper is a detailed comparison of this system for programmed placement pressure with a previous design which used load cell feedback to the computer to close the Z-Axis servo loop. It will be shown that the feed forward design is a cost saving performance enhancement. Performance enhancements directly related to this scheme include improvements in the following; reliability, repeatability of placement pressure, vacuum pressure, throughput efficiency, and spindle eccentricities.

articleTitle: Variable end-of-travel Sensor
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 1987 IEEE Southern Tier Technical Conference, 1987.
abstract: In a computer controlled machine, software time delays are used to all full travel of actuated mechanisms before continuing the sequence. When the end of travel of the actuated member is constant and the time for full travel is predictable, the software time delay is cost effective and throughput efficient. If the time of full actuation is variable the time delay must be long enough to allow for the worst case. This results in throughput inefficiency. This situation can be improved by using a switch or other similar sensor at stroke's end. This eliminates the need for time delays, but adds cost to the apparatus, and possibly reduces reliability. If the end of the travel is variable, however, a switch or position sensor is not viable and a time delay which is long enough to account for the fullest travel may be necessary. The only alternative to the time delay in variable end-of-travel situations is an economical, reliable motion sensor. This paper focuses on the development of an integrated, economical motion sensor for the parts centering arms in the placement head of the 4621A Omniplace Surface Mounted Component Assembly System. The sensor is termed integrated because of it's streamlined incorporation with structures already present in the head and is economical due to this integral nature. In addition to these attributes, it is expected to be reliable and performance enhancing. The variable end-of-travel sensor is based on a 10,000 turn solenoid with a cylindrical magnet which moves in the air gap. The EME produced by this transducer is amplified and presented to an absolute value comparator circuit. The open collector output of the comparator circuit is compatible with a current sourcing optically isolated computer input. The computer program executes the next sequential event upon determining end-of-centering arm motion in either direction. Thus, whether centering a small part (with greater travel) or a large part (with smaller travel) the next event after centering occurs with no delay. The previous design employed a time delay which allowed for reliable centering of the smallest part. This paper details the transducer and signal conditioning circuit, the improvement to throughput efficiency, and the cost effective integration of these elements into the existing design.

articleTitle: Communicating with Your Customers Determining Their Needs
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 1987 IEEE Southern Tier Technical Conference, 1987.
abstract: One of the more difficult aspects of providing a product to a customer is determining what the customer really needs. Frequently, the customer is not sure exactly what they need. They just have a problem and they are looking to you to provide the solution. The difficulty in determining product requirements is compounded by the fact that Test Design Automation (TDA) products need to be useful to a wide range of customers with diverse needs. That is the situation in which we found ourselves. TDA has the responsibility of supplying the IBM Corporation with its needed Test Generation and Fault Simulation capabilities. These products are software solutions designed to run on a wide range of general purpose system 370 computers under both VM and MVS operating systems. Our customer mix is a widely diverse set of product development groups; from the designers of the 3090 series in Poughkeepsie to a typewriter design group in Uxington, Kentucky. Not only is the product mix diverse, but also the geographic locations of the development groups. We serve product development labs worldwide. First, we had to be able to identify our "representative" customer. Once this was done we would need to open up more direct lines of communication with these customers. The method we used to improve upon these problems is the subject for this paper. It will cover the cross-section of the group which went about solving the problems; the methods chosen to attack the problems; implementation; and the mechanisms put into place to continue the work after the group's dissolution.

articleTitle: Binary Image Transforms: An old twist in Image Processing revisited
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 1987 IEEE Southern Tier Technical Conference, 1987.
abstract: Image processing techniques (and papers describing them) have evolved rapidly in recent years. Lately, publications in image processing have underscored advances in compression, restoration, and enhancement of gray level and color coded image information using dedicated pipeline processing and systolic array architectures. These new algorithms and specialized hardware have been developed and applied to such real-time tasks as automated testors on manufacturing lines and robotic vehicle guidance systems. Often overlooked is the part of binary image processing. A review of binary processing techniques is valuable in understanding the the basic operating principles of high-speed optical inspection devices in particular and many pipeline array processing devices in general. The class of binary image transforms covered here was originally developed for topological operations on threshold image data. These non-linear operations are based on boolean transformations of a pixel and its eight adjacent neighbors (in a discrete Cartesian plane) and are named morphological transforms by authors. A straightforward way to visualize such transforms is outlined in the paper and will be demonstrated at the conference. The demonstration program package was written using the IBM Personal Computer BASI language and was presented as an educational tool in a graduate level course in image processing. The skeletal program included in the text was enhanced to allow real-time demonstration of these transform techniques and encourages readers to experiment and develop their own lookup tables and image transforms. Understanding the function and generation of these lookup tables, which can provide any arbitrary boolean combination of the nine binary values available from a pixel and its eight Cartesian neighbors, is the key to grasping the image-transforms illustrated here. Examples in the paper and presentation give the reader an idea of the power and flexibility these transforms provide in image processing and feature recognition tasks. An overview of some relevant image processing topics precedes the discussion of binary transforms and the transform simulator.

articleTitle: Engineering Problem Analysis with Microcomputer Spreadsheets
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 1987 IEEE Southern Tier Technical Conference, 1987.
abstract: The use of microcomputers (personal computers) to solve Engineering related problems is a recent and rapidly growing phenomenon. A considerable amount of software by literally hundreds of vendors is available for purchase. The vendor software that is available is usually for the purpose of solving major engineering problems as opposed to the "single formula" problems that may require large amounts of data. However, these "single formula" problems can be very time consuming to solve, especially if the same formula is to be used repeatedly to calculate various reactions to varying data. For those engineers knowledgeable of computer programming, a simple solution is for them to write a program to find answers to their engineering problems. However, there are a considerable number of engineers who do not know, nor want to know, how to program a computer. For those individuals, a solution is to use microcomputer spreadsheets. No knowledge of formal programming is required, just the use of a microcomputer and the spreadsheet software. Spreadsheets can be conceptualized as a two dimensional mathematical matrix consisting of input data to a formula, and the relationships between the various data (the formula). Results can be in mathematical or graphical form. This paper provides an overview of microcomputer spreadsheets in general, and how these spreadsheets can be utilized to solve specific engineering related problems. Problem examples discussed are component reliability, component failure time distribution, and manufacturing interval estimation.

articleTitle: The MAP Pilot Project at IBM Endicott
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 1987 IEEE Southern Tier Technical Conference, 1987.
abstract: Endicott's Manufacturing Automation Protocol (MAP) pilot project demonstrates to the industry that IBM is seriously interested in MAP. Two software products, MAP Communication Server (MCS) and MAP Application Server (MAS), were developed in IBM Palo Alto, California, and demonstrated at the November 1985 Autofact show. In Endicott, IBM Series/1's (S/1) monitor various processes, used in the manufacturing of advanced circuit panels (ACP). Ultimately, MAP will significantly reduce the time required to develop software that will connect the programmable logic controllers (PLC) on the manufacturing floor and the IBM S/1's used to monitor the processes. A significant portion of the cost associated with new PLC installations is directly related to software. This cost will essentially be eliminated because MAP provides a standard interface. MAP will allow programmable logic controllers to communicate with each other and other computers directly, without requiring additional software. A broadband cable was installed in November of 1985, allowing both MAP and IBM PC Network to operate on the same physical cable. The MAP network connects the Series 1's on the manufacturing floor, while PC Network links IBM PC's between engineering offices. There are two gateways, an IBM PC/AT and an IBM S/1. The PC/AT gateway enables communication between MAP and PC Network, while host connections are possible via the S/1 gateway. IBM's MONACO (Monitoring and Control) and PC Graphics were modified to operate on the MAP network. IBM MONACO is the software product residing in the S/1, used for process monitoring. It is a program product that was developed in Sindelfingen, W. Germany. IBM PC Graphics was developed, for internal use, in Endicott and displays the data collected by MONACO on an IBM PC/XT or PC/AT color monitor. Both MONACO and PC Graphics are used at other IBM locations. By accessing the Series/l on the manufacturing floor, real time process data, including color graphic data displays, will be available in engineering offices, conference rooms, and classrooms. This same data could also be made available to a control center. Today, MAP is receiving both national and international attention. This large scale effort was initiated by the customers of PLC manufacturers because these customers were overwhelmed with the number of proprietary islands of automation and information. MAP, on the broadband cable, is the standard that will make this data more readily accessible, provide single terminal access and reduce cable costs.

articleTitle: Software Development - from Concept to Completion
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 1987 IEEE Southern Tier Technical Conference, 1987.
abstract: A large software development project is described with the steps taken toward completion. The software system was developed to support a new testing technology for digital computer designers. This software system was also required to fit into an existing, complex design automation system in IBM. The history of this design automation project over a three-year period and its characteristics are presented. The techniques used in development from initial modeling and requirement definition through shipment of code to the customers are identified. Techniques included are: development documentation, project planning, technical review meetings, automated testing tools, and formal inspections. Also discussed are some lessons learned. Changing requirements were all too common. While project planning was key, the critical factor was component staging from specification and development through testing and shipment. Management and technical awareness of the challenges were achieved through technical meetings. This led to the realization that the development process must change. Management and development perspectives were blended in this paper.

articleTitle: On the Optimization of Search Heuristics: a Fuzzy Approach
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 1987 IEEE Southern Tier Technical Conference, 1987.
abstract: Heuristics are key factors in reducing the computational workload of searching decision trees. Artificial intelligence techniques utilize algorithms which are highly dependent upon the heuristic sensitivity and the processing workload required to generate the plausibility of a given node. Fuzzy set theory offers a means of providing reasonable heuristics to the search procedure in an effort to improve overall heuristic performance. A procedure was defined to generate fuzzy heuristics for an nth order state-space system. Results indicate that although the fuzzy heuristic is more sensitive than a linear-weighted test heuristic and may be beneficial for certain applications, the defuzzification algorithm required by the fuzzy approach required increased computational efforts. A brief review of Al search techniques is provided as well as an illustrative example which compares the performance of the fuzzy heuristic versus a linear-weighted test heuristic.

articleTitle: Innovative Helical Wrap Installation of Fiber Optic Cable
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 1987 IEEE Southern Tier Technical Conference, 1987.
abstract: A fiber optic link, spun helically onto a phase conductor and lightning shield (static) wire of an existing 115KV transmission line, replaces an unreliable direct current pilot wire relay channel in a developmental project of the NYSEG Corporation. The resulting installation, now completed, was the first of its kind in the U.S. and is the first anywhere that employs a fiber cable helically wrapped around a lightning shield wire.

articleTitle: Gummel-Poon Model Parameter Optimization for a Power Transistor
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 1987 IEEE Southern Tier Technical Conference, 1987.
abstract: Computer Aided Design and Analysis tools rely heavily on accurate device models. The development of an accurate PNP power transistor model is presented in this paper. The device is modeled in terms of the Gummel-Poon model. It is difficult to obtain accurate values for the parameters due to the complexity of the model and the inherent assumptions and inaccuracies in the measurement procedure. Optimizing the parameter values through trial and error is not easy and a more systematic and efficient method is presented. An interactive design optimization program called DESIGN is used to adjust the parameter values so that the measured and the predicted output characteristics match at selected values of base current. The result is an accurate model that is sophisticated enough to predict the complex behavior of the transistor.

articleTitle: Optical Detection of Bent Pins in a High-Density Array
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 1987 IEEE Southern Tier Technical Conference, 1987.
abstract: This paper describes a prototype system being developed for the detection of bent pins on a high density integrated circuit module. It is a noncontact approach that relies on the detection of the specific optical diffraction patterns that result when laser light shines on a bent pin. As the module pins are passed through a fixed laser beam, the diffraction patterns are captured by an area optical array which is continuously scanned by a dedicated processor. If a bent pin is detected and the motion of the pin array is known, the approximate location of the bent pin can be determined by triangulation based on multiple passes. Information revealing the angle of bend in the scanning plane is imbedded in the diffraction pattern.

articleTitle: Utility Application of Static Var-Compensation
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 1987 IEEE Southern Tier Technical Conference, 1987.
abstract: The Marcy South Project, 200 miles of 345KV (kilovolts) transmission lines, is being constructed to permit the cost-effective north-south transfer of low cost hydro-produced power from Canada, downstate to New York City by 1988. This project has involved new and interesting technology in its design and construction. One such technology, soon to be implemented at New York State Electric Gas (NYSEG), on a scale unprecedented in North America, is the Static Var Compensator (SVC). This paper describes NYSEG's SVC, a multi-million dollar power electronics technology not only new to NYSEG, but relatively new to the entire electric power industry. The various component parts of the SVC are discussed: thyristor valves, high voltage shunt capacitors, shunt reactors, harmonic filters, and the microcomputer controller. Basically, a gigantic parallel tuned circuit at 345KV, the SVC will regulate the voltage and enhance damping of power system oscillations, by controlling reactive power flow on the Bulk Power Transmission System in the area of Fraser, New York, in NYSEG's Oneonta District. This regulation and damping ability is critical to the stability and operability of the New York State Bulk Power System at the high levels of power transfer anticipated.

articleTitle: Programmable Placement Pressure in a Placement Head for Surface Mounted Devices
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 1987 IEEE Southern Tier Technical Conference, 1987.
abstract: Due to the broad spectrum of lead configurations of surface mount components and the variation in adhesive viscosities, various placement pressures are required. A proper adhesive meniscus must be achieved during application of components to adhesive dots to insure good lead to pad contact. This paper focuses on the development of a programmable placement pressure system which is a feature of the 4621A Omniplace Surface Mount component Placement System. A commercially available pressure regulator is programmed with a DAC to produce the required back pressure for a piston activated compliant placement spindle. Coinciding with this, the Z axis servo system drives the placement spindle to the desired Placement location. When the component, which is held by vacuum on the placement spindle, makes contact with the printed circuit board, a switch is activated. The computer receives the switch input as a signal to stop the Z axis drive. Pressure overshoot is avoided by the fast response time of the pressure regulator which controls the piston and the unique control algorithm which was developed. Included in this paper is a detailed comparison of this system for programmed placement pressure with a previous design which used load cell feedback to the computer to close the Z-Axis servo loop. It will be shown that the feed forward design is a cost saving performance enhancement. Performance enhancements directly related to this scheme include improvements in the following; reliability, repeatability of placement pressure, vacuum pressure, throughput efficiency, and spindle eccentricities.

articleTitle: Variable End-of-Travel Sensor
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 1987 IEEE Southern Tier Technical Conference, 1987.
abstract: In a computer controlled machine, software time delays are used to allow full travel of actuated mechanisms before continuing the sequence. When the end of travel of the actuated member is constant and the time for full travel is predictable, the software time delay is cost effective and throughput efficient. If the time of full actuation is variable the time delay must be long enough to allow for the worst case. This results in throughput inefficiency. This situation can be improved by using a switch or other similar sensor at stroke's end. This eliminates the need for time delays, but adds cost to the apparatus, and possibly reduces reliability. If the end of the travel is variable, however, a switch or position sensor is not viable and a time delay which is long enough to account for the fullest travel may be necessary. The only alternative to the time delay in variable end-of-travel situations is an economical, reliable motion sensor. This paper focuses on the development of an integrated, economical motion sensor for the parts centering arms in the placement head of the 4621A Omniplace Surface Mounted Component Assembly System. The sensor is termed integrated because of it's streamlined incorporation with structures already present in the head and is economical due to this integral nature. In addition to these attributes, it is expected to be reliable and performance enhancing. The variable end-of-travel sensor is based on a 10,000 turn solenoid with a cylindrical magnet which moves in the air gap. The EMF produced by this transducer is amplified and presented to an absolute value comparator circuit. The open collector output of the comparator circuit is compatible with a current sourcing optically isolated computer input. The computer program executes the next sequential event upon determining end-of-centering arm motion in either direction. Thus, whether centering a small part (with greater travel) or a large part (with smaller travel) the next event after centering occurs with no delay. The previous design employed a time delay which allowed for reliable centering of the smallest part. This paper details the transducer and signal conditioning circuit, the improvement to throughput efficiency, and the cost effective integration of these elements into the existing design.

articleTitle: Innovative Variable Mesh Simulator
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 1987 IEEE Southern Tier Technical Conference, 1987.
abstract: A valuable design to aid designers of digitial computer circuits is a "good" logic simulator. Because the digital hardware technology has advanced rapidly over recent years (i.e., more and more logic gates on a single chip), faster and easier to use logic simulators capable of handling large, complex digital circuits are continually in demand. An important milestone in meeting this demand was the development of the Innovative Variable Mesh Simulator (IVMS). The IVMS program is based on the flat model approach and permits interactive or batch processing. An earlier logic simulator called the Variable Mesh Simulator (VMS) is based on the hierarchical model approach and only permits batch processing. The use of the flat model approach in IVMS instead of the hierarchical approach in VMS results in a faster simulation for the same application. In addition to the processing advantages, interactive IVMS provides logic designers with the means to debug within a short period of time both the test case problems and the structure (the overall design and/or the behavior models). IVMS permits the user to explore various model changes and/or stimuli changes with the resulting output effects while in, the same session. A more detailed description of the IVMS program development is given in this paper, including a comparsion of the flat model and hierarchical models' approaches of simulator construction. The key features of the MS program, including some examples of performance data, are also described.

articleTitle: On the Optimal Pulse Control of an Electric Drive
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 1987 IEEE Southern Tier Technical Conference, 1987.
abstract: Results on the application of an optimal control technique in microprocessor-based position control system with a DC motor are presented. The technique is based on the use of optimal control signals corresponding to various "typical" initial conditions, defined during the system design and stored in a look-up table. A numerical procedure for the definition of optimal control signals is proposed.

articleTitle: A Generalized Approach for Automatic Test Pattern Generation
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 1987 IEEE Southern Tier Technical Conference, 1987.
abstract: A generalized approach for designing fault simulators using a library of simulation primitives is presented in this paler. A comprehensive set of simulation primitives has been developed using C programming language on the IBM PC. This library of simulation primitives has been used in realizing a fault simulator for automatic test pattern generation in combinational logic circuits. The fault simulator employs a combination of random pattern generation, concurrent fault simulation, and FAN algorithm for generating the complete set of test vectors to cover all the faults in the fault dictionary of the circuit under test. The library of simulation primitives is general enough to facilitate the development of fault simulators using any other test algorithms such as DALG or PODEM.

articleTitle: Fatigue and Creep in Solder Joints
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 1987 IEEE Southern Tier Technical Conference, 1987.
abstract: With the advent of surface mount components, many packaging engineers have been trying to determine the critical performance parameters for the technology. From first principals, the shear strain on a joint will be decreased if the distance between the components is increased. A simple way to do this is to increase the solder volume of the connection then fatigue cycle the parts to failure. The above experiment was performed with four different chip capacitors and six different solder volumes. The tests data confirmed a very consistent and predictable increase in fatigue life with solder joint height. Another item of interest to a package design engineer is how failures are initiated in a surface mount package. The usual assumption is that the only cause for failure is due to fatigue from dissimilar expansion coefficients of the components. Experiments have been performed the show solder cracking will occur in the solder due to the difference in expansion coefficients between the solder and component. No external loading is necessary. The size of the joint may have to be considered to minimize the problem.

articleTitle: On the Stability Analysis of an Adaptive Control System with a Simplified Control Procedure
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 1987 IEEE Southern Tier Technical Conference, 1987.
abstract: This paper presents the results on the stability analysis of computer-based control systems with the simplified adaptation procedure implemented through look-up tables and special selection rules. The simplified procedure implies the development of a number of controllers during the system design, representation of the controllers by a look-up table, and implementation of a procedure for the selection of the appropriate entry of a look-up table during the system operation. Systems, implementing the procedure, can be considered as systems with nonlinearity so that some specific stability problems have to be investigated. The paper presents the analysis of the transient processes in the system causes by the controller change, and the selection of the admissible difference between the alternative controllers in the look-up table. The analytical technique employed to the stability problem in the paper is based on Liapunov's second method. Since the considered nonlinearity type meets Aizerman's conditions, a Liapunov function in so-called "Quadratic Plus Integral" was used. Following the general procedure of Liapunov's method, the absolute stability conditions were formulated for the considered type of control systems.

articleTitle: A Computer Controlled Aircraft Defense System (CCADS)
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 1987 IEEE Southern Tier Technical Conference, 1987.
abstract: The problems and complexities of defending military aircraft from hostile forces are described. Many different types of weapon systems may be encountered, requiring rapid, accurate countermeasures for survival. It is shown how computer generation of a tactical situation display and computer control of aircraft sensors and countermeasures enhances aircraft survival, compared to autonomous or manual approaches.

articleTitle: Communicating with Your Customers Determining Their Needs
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 1987 IEEE Southern Tier Technical Conference, 1987.
abstract: One of the more difficult aspects of providing a product to a customer is determining what the customer really needs. Frequently, the customer is not sure exactly what they need. They just have a problem and they are looking to you to provide the solution. The difficulty in determining product requirements is compounded by the fact that Test Design Automation (TDA) products need to be useful to a wide range of customers with diverse needs. That is the situation in which we found ourselves. TDA has the responsibility of supplying the IBM Corporation with its needed Test Generation and Fault Simulation capabilities. These products are software solutions designed to run on a wide range of general purpose system 370 computers under both VM and MVS operating systems. Our customer mix is a widely diverse set of product development groups; from the designers of the 3090 series in Poughkeepsie to a typewriter design group in Lexington, Kentucky. Not only is the product mix diverse, but also the geographic locations of the development groups. We serve product development labs worldwide. First, we had to be able to identify our "representative" customer. Once this was done we would need to open up more direct lines of communication with these customers. The method we used to improve upon these problems is the subject for this paper. It will cover the cross-section of the group which went about solving the problems; the methods chosen to attack the problems; implementation; and the mechanisms put into place to continue the work after the group's dissolution.

articleTitle: Computer Machine Control Language Development
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 1987 IEEE Southern Tier Technical Conference, 1987.
abstract: This paper presents the architecture, structure, and general development of a computer machine control language. A specific language development is presented for a general purpose educational robot. The machine control primitives are identified and defined. The necessary functional control of the robot is identified and the primitives are used to derive secondary control expressions at a higher level. The utility of the higher level language is used for support, control, sensing, and development, while the machine primitive manipulation is delegated to lower levels of the language hierarchy. This approach to developing the computer control software bridges the gap between the convenience and efficiency of the high level user support and the labor of manipulating the machine control and sensing primitives.

articleTitle: Speech Recognition: A Tutorial on the Subject
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 1987 IEEE Southern Tier Technical Conference, 1987.
abstract: The unnatural form of communication that one must use in interaction with a computer has prompted much research in the area of voice recognition. There have been enormous amounts of research in this area in the past decade. This paper presents a simplified overview of the linguistics and system approach behind speech recognition systems, so that those unfamiliar with this area may obtain a generalized understanding of the setbacks, achievements and operation of the verbal interface.

articleTitle: Designing Testable Plas for both Offline Testing and Concurrent Error Detection
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 1987 IEEE Southern Tier Technical Conference, 1987.
abstract: In this paper, we present an improved design of testable PLAs for offline testing and suggest a unified approach for both offline testing and Concurrent Error Detection (CED). This design offers a more efficient use of the additional hardware required for designing testable PLAs. The additional hardware required includes an address decoder [1] to select or deselect the product lines of the PLA, a ripple counter to generate the address for the decoder, and a Totally Self Checking (TSC) checker for the output lines of the PLA. The design requires only two additional pinouts on the chip in contrast to (1og/sub 2/(m+l), + 1) additional pinouts [1], where m is the number of product lines in the PLA. The additional hardware used for CED is also effectively utilized during offline testing, and the design is suitable for built-in testing of PLAs. The test procedures cover all single mode stuck-at, bridging, and crosspoint faults.

articleTitle: Binary Image Transforms: An old twist in Image Processing revisited
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 1987 IEEE Southern Tier Technical Conference, 1987.
abstract: Image processing techniques (and papers describing them) have evolved rapidly in recent years. Lately, publications in image processing have underscored advances in compression, restoration, and enhancement of gray level and color coded image information using dedicated pipeline processing and systolic array architectures. These new algorithms and specialized hardware have been developed and applied to such real-time tasks as automated testors on manufacturing lines and robotic vehicle guidance systems. Often overlooked is the art of binary image processing. A review of binary processing techniques is valuable in understanding the the basic operating principles of high-speed optical inspection devices in particular and many pipeline array processing devices in general. The class of binary image transforms covered here was originally developed for topological operations on thresheld image data. These non-linear operations are based on boolean transformations of a pixel and its eight adjacent neighbors (in a discrete Cartesian plane) and are named morphological transforms by some authors. A straightforward way to visualize such transforms is outlined in the paper and will be demonstrated at the conference. The demonstration program package was written using the IBM Personal Computer BASIC language and was presented as an educational tool in a graduate level course in image processing. The skeletal program included in the text was enhanced to allow real-time demonstration of these transform techniques and encourages readers to experiment and develop their own lookup tables and image transforms. Understanding the function and generation of these lookup tables, which can provide any arbitrary boolean combination of the nine binary values available from a pixel and its eight Cartesian neighbors, is the key to grasping the image transforms illustrated here. Examples in the paper and presentation give the reader an idea of the power and flexibility these transforms provide in image processing and feature recognition tasks. An overview of some relevant image processing topics precedes the discussion of binary transforms and the transform simulator.
